title: Four finite-level rectangle corners
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a Cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$ proper, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to Y'$. Use the constant coefficient datum $\Lambda,I,P_n=\Lambda/I^n$ and reductions of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum], and let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, with the small sites and derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each scheme $T$ write $\Lambda_T,(P_n)_T$ for the constant sheaves. All operations below are the ordinary uncompleted derived module operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], using the canonical constant-coefficient identifications $u^{-1}\Lambda_V\cong\Lambda_U$ for each arrow $u:U\to V$ of the square. Tensor products are over the constant sheaf on the relevant scheme [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Reductions are regarded as $\Lambda$-objects by restriction of scalars, as in the coefficient datum.

Put $E=L(g')^*K\in D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. For every $n\geq1$ define four objects of $D(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_n&:=Lg^*((Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Y}(P_n)_Y),&
B_n&:=Lg^*(Rf_*K_n),\\
C_n&:=(Rf'_*E)\otimes^L_{\Lambda_{Y'}}(P_n)_{Y'},&
D_n&:=Rf'_*(E_n),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(P_n)_X$ and $E_n:=L(g')^*K_n$. Equip this definition with the canonical identification
$$
E_n\xrightarrow{\sim}E\otimes^L_{\Lambda_{X'}}(P_n)_{X'}
$$
obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the constant-coefficient comparison. The Cartesian identification used throughout is the natural isomorphism
$$
L(g')^*Lf^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(f')^*Lg^*,
$$
formed by the inverse of $c_{g',f}$ followed by $c_{f',g}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], identifying $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$ through $\alpha$. Equalities between these expressions in the blueprint mean these specified canonical isomorphisms.

proof.text: For any arrow $u:U\to V$ of the square and commutative ring $R$, the ring-sheaf inverse image has the ring adjunction: use the pro-etale inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] (whose inverse image preserves finite limits, since it is a morphism of sites) and its finite-product-preserving lift [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-group-ring-objects], interpreting ring sheaves as ring objects by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]. For a ring sheaf $F$ on $U$, [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections] gives natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(u^{-1}R_V,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R_V,u_*F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{CRing}}(R,(u_*F)(V))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{CRing}}(R,F(U))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R_U,F)$. The middle equality uses the direct-image formula and $U\times_VV\cong U$. Write $\Phi_F$ for this bijection. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] with $A=u^{-1}R_V$ and $B=R_U$: it gives an isomorphism $\theta:R_U\to u^{-1}R_V$ and $\Phi_F(a)=a\circ\theta$. For the structure map $c^u_R:u^{-1}R_V\to R_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], its adjunct sends each constant section $r$ to the same constant section $r$. Thus $\Phi_{R_U}(c^u_R)=1_{R_U}$, so $c^u_R\circ\theta=1_{R_U}$ and $c^u_R=\theta^{-1}$. Use this specified structure map as the isomorphism $u^{-1}R_V\cong R_U$; the displayed bijections show naturality in $R$. Thus the identifications for $R=\Lambda$ and $R=P_n$ commute with $\Lambda\to P_n$. For composable arrows $u:U\to V$, $v:V\to W$, identify $(v\circ u)^{-1}$ with $u^{-1}v^{-1}$. The adjuncts of $c^{v\circ u}_R$ and $c^u_R\circ u^{-1}(c^v_R)$ are both maps $R_W\to(v\circ u)_*R_U$ sending $r$ to its constant section on $U\times_W Z$ for every object $Z$ on $W$. The constant-sheaf Hom bijection makes these adjuncts equal; injectivity of the adjunction makes the comparisons equal. For the identity arrow, the same bijection identifies the adjunct with the identity map, giving the identity comparison.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], module pullback with the ring identifications of step 1 is exact, and $Lu^*$ is its termwise derived functor. Naturality of those identifications in $\Lambda\to P_n$ identifies $L(g')^*(P_n)_X$ with $(P_n)_{X'}$ in degree zero, with the correct $\Lambda_{X'}$-action. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $K$ and $(P_n)_X$. With the reduction definition of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum] this gives $L(g')^*K_n\cong L(g')^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_{X'}}(P_n)_{X'}$. Define $E=L(g')^*K$, $E_n=L(g')^*K_n$ and retain this isomorphism. All objects and comparisons here are taken after restriction to $\Lambda$-coefficients; no exchange of pushforward with restriction of scalars is used.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), specialized to constant ring sheaves

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum] for $K_n$ and [def-weil-derived-tensor] for reduction on $Y$ and $Y'$. The source and target categories in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] show that $Rf_*K$ and $Rf_*K_n$ are objects on $Y$, that their indicated reductions and pullbacks give $A_n,B_n$ on $Y'$, and that $Rf'_*E$ and $Rf'_*E_n$ are on $Y'$, giving $C_n,D_n$. These are exactly the four displayed definitions, all in $D(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. Only the operations and their domains are being composed; no projection formula or base-change isomorphism is asserted here.

source.place: display defining A_n, B_n, C_n, D_n

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], the chosen $\alpha$ gives $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$. The constant coefficient identifications are compatible with composition by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] applies to $(h,k)=(g',f)$ and $(f',g)$. The composite $(c_{g',f})^{-1}$, the identification of the common composite arrow, and $c_{f',g}$ is the specified natural isomorphism $L(g')^*Lf^*\cong L(f')^*Lg^*$ from $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ to $D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. This fixes the Cartesian identification used by the definition; it does not assume that the two composites of functors are literally equal.
